precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, forget your pain; the Bible says, “Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.” The bottle says, numb your sorrow. Christ answers that lie: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

The bottle offers to carry your burden for you. It talks to you like scripture in a dark room with one light over the table: drink me, I can take away thy sorrows; you're depressed, don't worry about it; you're stressed out, put the kids to bed early and drink me. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

Christ is the one who actually takes the weight. The labouring and heavy laden are told to come to him, not to the liquor store, and he gives rest. The bottle only numbs the sorrow until tomorrow; casting the burden on the Lord is how he sustains you and keeps the righteous from being moved.

precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, you are a failure. You ain't nothing. You're going to be the same person you always were. The Bible says: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

Guess what? You can repent. The bottle says you're a failure; the Bible says you can repent and become a new man.

But it starts with acknowledging it: I'm an alcoholic. I'm a fornicator, an adulterer, a liar, a thief; I deal with envy, covetousness, idolatry. That is where the change happens. And acknowledging it is not enough; you have to work on fixing those things. You can't say, I'm an alcoholic, and keep going out drinking.

No condemnation belongs to those who walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. The man chained to the bottle is walking after the flesh; the man who casts his burden on the Lord and walks in the Spirit is free of the condemnation the bottle keeps whispering over him.

precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, you can't change. You're the same; you're going to be that same person. The Bible says, “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.”

The law of the Lord converts the soul: it changes a man. So the lie that you can't change is answered by the perfect law of God. You can repent and become a new man.

That is the other side of casting your burden on the Lord. You don't just hand him the weight; you take on his law, and his law turns you into somebody different. The bottle keeps you drunk and stupid, the way the enemy wants it, with a liquor store in every black neighborhood and weed stores everywhere to keep you high, drunk and stupid. The law of the Lord makes the simple wise and converts the soul out of that.

precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, take another drink. You can handle it; drink some more. The Bible says, “And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.”

The bottle wants to fill you: drink me and be filled with my love. It says, you're alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. I love you more than water. You don't need to eat today; I'll make the food taste better. You can't sleep; I can put you to sleep so fast you won't even realize it. The bottle starts talking like scripture: I am that I am, the comfort of them all.

That is excess, and it destroys the body too. Alcohol builds fat around your organs and your belly, raises your risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and type two diabetes, makes you hungrier and drives you to fast food. Four or five shots a drink every day is thousands of calories a week, and then you wonder why you can't lose weight or climb a flight of stairs.

The command is to be filled with something else: the Spirit. Cast your burden on the Lord and be filled with his Spirit, not with the bottle.

precepts.text: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart; softer than oil, yet drawn swords. The missionaries came into Africa speaking the love of white Jesus, learned our strengths and weaknesses, then devastated us with colonialism and slavery. They taught us to read but not to reason, which is why people cannot reconcile Romans 9:13 with John 3:16. Kwame Nkrumah wanted one visa and one gold-backed currency for the continent, and the CIA ran him out.
precepts.point: He parted his kingdom among his servants while he lived: Ptolemy took Egypt, Lysimachus Thrace and Asia Minor, Seleucus Syria, Cassander Macedonia. What he held united, they could not.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
The Greeks and then the Europeans divided the land for gain. David shows how they got in: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

When the white man comes, his words are smoother than butter. He will talk about Jesus, about love, about honour and respect, and you will fall in love with what he says. But his intent all along was war and to destroy you.

They did not come into Africa talking war. They came with missionaries who talked the love of white Jesus: we love you, dusty Africans. In Africa you have Hamites and Shemites; the Shemites are the Bantus, and the Nilotes are the Hamites, who were their mercenaries. They brought their religions, spoke words of peace, learned our strengths and our weaknesses, and then devastated us with colonialism and slavery. That is how they divided Africa for financial gain, and why Africa is not united today.

Kwame Nkrumah wanted to unite the entire continent with one visa and one financial system backed by gold. The CIA said, we got to get rid of this dude, and he was run out of Ghana to Guinea.

They taught us to read but not to reason. That is why people get confused over Romans 9:13 and John 3:16: they can read, but they cannot reason. Softer than oil, yet drawn swords: behind every smooth word, the intent was war.

precepts.text: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart.
precepts.point: We took sweet counsel together and walked unto the house of God in company. The betrayer is the officer beside you, the man you picked up for Sabbath.

note.label: Destroyed by Familiar Hands

precepts.why:
“For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it.” It was not the enemy that set David up, or he would have been ready, because he knows who the enemy is. “But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance. We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company.” It was the man he trusted, the man he went fishing with, and that took him by surprise. Later in the same psalm David describes that man: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

A man mine equal: an officer of ten, of twenty, of fifty, just like me. We took sweet counsel together: Deacon, I need counsel; Captain, what do you think about this? But while he was taking counsel, he was plotting. Some are plotting to take your wife: she is too beautiful for him. Some are plotting to take your position at the job you brought them into, telling the white man, give me his position. I picked him up every Sabbath and every Wednesday, and when he came to betray me he had no problem doing it.

“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” Christ was betrayed that way: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Today we do not kiss, but we dap: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That smooth greeting can be the betrayal. In 2018 a man who sat in another man's house, barbecued and travelled with him, came and took all his furniture and put his children to sleep on the cold floor.

Jeremiah warns: “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” Supplant means betray, plot. Other camps slander our members and leadership, because they know our people believe anything without proof; they are Esau in black skin, who “have taught their tongue to speak lies.” They come asking to fellowship, but we are not stupid.

It was not the enemy that killed Thomas Sankara; it was his best friend, who grew up with him. It was Maduro's own handpicked bodyguards who stood down and handed him over, taking American money instead of a bullet for him. That is war in the heart behind smooth words. David is telling you: do not fall asleep.

precepts.text: The wicked go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.
precepts.point: America embargoed Venezuela for twenty years before blaming Maduro for the suffering.

note.label: Destroyed by Familiar Hands

precepts.why:
“He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.” Venezuela is a peaceful country. America put an embargo and sanctions on Venezuela for twenty years to destroy its economy; the money goes down, everything goes down. Then twenty years later: he is a drug dealer, he is this, he is that; people of Venezuela, we can change your lives. America did that. “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart.”

Only the simple will believe it was about drug trafficking. Trump pardoned one of the biggest drug dealers a couple of months before, and Mexico, on America's border, has more drug cartels than any place in the world. Then the story shifted to oil. They use the same stupidity because they know some black people will believe that garbage. Ninety-nine point nine percent of the words that come out of the Trump mouth are a lie. He lies even when he is not talking; he is blinking and lying, and every person who works for him too.

David shows why: “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.” The little baby is born, he does not even talk yet, and he is looking at you lying. That is Trump: before he can say a word he already starts lying. All of them. God said it, not me: it is in them to be liars. And our people believe them, because they are white. Who told you the white man cannot lie?

Habakkuk describes the same man, whose “soul which is lifted up is not upright in him.” Esau is not right: “he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home”: he is in everybody's business, with bases around the world used to overthrow any government that does not do what he says. He destroys the economy with sanctions, sends in CIA agitators and propaganda to raise the people up, and then comes back as the good guy offering to help. Like a man who rapes a woman and then offers to take her to therapy.

That is putting forth his hands against such as be at peace with him. The wicked go astray from the womb speaking lies, and his smooth words always have war in his heart.

precepts.text: His words were smoother than butter but war was in his heart; this wicked is Esau.
precepts.point: Esau does not regard the operations of the Most High; they want to be as God, above God, in their sciences and everything their hands touch. But the wicked, whether Esau or our own people, will not be built back up once destroyed. When those bombs hit, they are gone.

note.label: Psalm 28: Be Not Silent To Me

precepts.why:
“Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity, which speak peace to their neighbours, but mischief is in their hearts.” Here is that wicked: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

Words smoother than butter, but war in his heart; this wicked is Esau. Some wickedness is visible and clear, like homosexuality, but there is wickedness you will not pick up on as easily, peace in the mouth and mischief in the heart, and men are judged for it. David is giving clues about the different types of wicked that will be judged.

precepts.text: He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him; he hath broken his covenant.
precepts.point: Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.” Psalm 55 shows the same man: “He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.” He puts forth his hands against those at peace with him and breaks his covenant. That is the deceitful working of the razor tongue: peace in the mouth, and a broken covenant behind it.

precepts.text: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart; the white man promises reparations and forty acres and a mule, but breaks his covenant.
precepts.point: Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.” That is the tongue like a sharp razor, working deceitfully. The white man promises reparations and forty acres and a mule, words smoother than butter and softer than oil, but war is in his heart and he breaks his covenant. His soft words are drawn swords.

precepts.text: The eyes of the Most High are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers.
precepts.point: The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
David asks, “Give ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.” The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. “For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.” His eyes are over the righteous and his ears are open to their prayers, but his face is against them that do evil.

You have to put yourself in the Bible and see yourself in these scriptures, the way Elder Kena, Bishop and the leadership men teach. David mourns because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked who cast iniquity upon him; if we want to be heard the way he was, we have to be among the righteous.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments as He commanded.
precepts.point: The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why: What is righteousness? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments as he commanded. The eyes of the Lord are over the righteous and his ears open to their prayers, so keeping the commandments is how our prayer gets his ear. That is how David could ask the Most High to attend unto him and hear him.

precepts.text: He that serveth the Most High is accepted with favor and his prayer reaches unto the clouds, and the prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds.
precepts.point: The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“He that serveth the Lord shall be accepted with favour, and his prayer shall reach unto the clouds. The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds: and till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.” He that serves the Most High is accepted with favour, and his prayer reaches unto the clouds. The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds and will not depart until the most High beholds and executes judgment.

That is David's prayer in Psalm 55, mourning and making a noise because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked. His ears are open to the prayers of the righteous, and the prayer of the humble servant does not stop until he judges.

precepts.text: Among these nations thou shalt find no ease; the Most High gives a trembling heart, failing eyes, sorrow of mind, and thy life hangs in doubt.
precepts.point: The fearfulness and trembling and horror are written in the curses, the curses we did not learn in the Christian church. Many of the scriptures come back to these curses.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“My heart is sore pained within me: and the terrors of death are fallen upon me. Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, and horror hath overwhelmed me.” That fearfulness, trembling and horror are written in the curses: “among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind: And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”.

These are the curses we did not learn in the Christian church, and many of the scriptures come back to them. Think about the condition we are in today: even keeping the commandments, we still suffer the same oppression, though the Most High covers those that keep them. When you drive, police will still jump behind you and run your plates, so make sure your tags are legal and not expired. A trembling heart and a life hanging in doubt is where David's heart is in Psalm 55.

precepts.text: We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom, and the four chapters a day is part of that exhortation to continue in the faith.
precepts.point: Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Oh that I had wings like a dove! for then would I fly away, and be at rest.” When these things come upon us, many times you would think, if I could just get away, just leave this place. But the scriptures say we must serve out this punishment: Paul and Barnabas were “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.”

We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom. The four chapters a day is part of that exhortation to continue in the faith. Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield. There is no flying away from it; we endure it into the kingdom.

precepts.text: Whoever leaves house or family for the gospel receives a hundredfold now with persecutions, and in the world to come eternal life.
precepts.point: Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
David would hasten his escape from the windy storm and tempest. Christ says what comes to the one who stays in the faith: “There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel’s, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.”

A hundredfold now, with persecutions, and in the world to come eternal life. The persecutions come with it; we must through much tribulation enter the kingdom, and we serve out this punishment rather than fly away. But the rest David wished for is promised at the end of it.

precepts.text: My people is risen up as an enemy, pulling off the robe and garment from them that pass by, like stealing a man's starter jacket or gym shoes.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues: for I have seen violence and strife in the city.” This is us being cursed in the city. “Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely as men averse from war.” The Most High's own people are risen up as an enemy, pulling off the robe and garment from them that pass by, like stealing a man's starter jacket or his gym shoes.

You want to hasten your escape because you open the doors and go out into the world to work, shop or school, and there is all this strife among our people. Moses dealt with the same thing when he left Pharaoh's house and found two men fighting.

precepts.text: The Most High has a controversy with the land for lying, killing, and stealing, black on black crime, so the land mourns and everyone in it languishes.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” The Most High has a controversy with the land for the lying, killing and stealing, black on black crime, blood touching blood. That is the violence and strife David saw in the city, the mischief and sorrow in the midst of it.

“Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.” The land mourns and everyone in it languishes. This is us cursed in the city.

precepts.text: They make haste to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are iniquity and wasting and destruction are in their paths.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why: “Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; wasting and destruction are in their paths.” Day and night they go about the city upon the walls; they make haste to shed innocent blood, their thoughts are iniquity, and wasting and destruction are in their paths. That is the wickedness in the midst of the city, where deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

precepts.text: Take fast hold of instruction and avoid the path of the wicked, for they sleep not unless they cause some to fall.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life. Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men. Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.” In a city full of violence and strife, take fast hold of instruction and avoid the path of the wicked altogether.

“For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.” That is why day and night they go about it upon the walls: they cannot sleep unless they have done mischief and caused some to fall. Instruction is thy life; hold it fast and turn from their way.

precepts.text: Seek in the streets for a man that executes judgment and seeks truth; He struck them but they refused correction and to return.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it.” Seek in the streets for a man that executes judgment and seeks truth. In David's city, deceit and guile depart not from her streets, and it is the same in ours.

“O Lord, are not thine eyes upon the truth? thou hast stricken them, but they have not grieved; thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return.” He struck them, but they have not grieved; they refused correction and refused to return. That is why the violence and strife stay in the city: we are cursed in it and have not turned.

precepts.text: Ahithophel, King David's own counselor, left him and joined Absalom's conspiracy to steal the kingdom, and that is betrayal.
precepts.point: This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it”. It was a man his equal, his guide and his acquaintance. That is Ahithophel: “Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong”. King David's own counsellor left him and joined Absalom's conspiracy to steal the kingdom. “And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O Lord, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.”

That is betrayal, by someone he took sweet counsel with and walked with to the house of God. Betrayal by someone you know well cuts where an enemy's reproach could not. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth.
